props.title: Hyatt Regency Denver at Colorado Convention Center
props.lede: Hyatt Regency Denver is the big hotel connected to the Colorado Convention Center, with 1,100 guest rooms and the largest hotel ballroom in the state.

headingText.html: A lot of the conference receptions, awards dinners and company parties in Denver happen here, along with big weddings, and the rooftop terrace looks out over the skyline.

props.title: Live music in each Hyatt Regency Denver event space
props.lede: Here’s the act we’d pick for each space. Press play to hear it over the photo.

spaces.name: Denver City Terrace
spaces.facts: The Denver City Terrace is a rooftop with views of the skyline, about 3,500 sq ft, for up to 300 guests. The hotel holds wedding ceremonies up there.
spaces.why: A solo violin to a full string quartet, from the ceremony through dinner.
spaces.alt: A long high-top table set for dinner on the Denver City Terrace, with the convention center behind.

spaces.name: Centennial Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Centennial Ballroom is about 30,000 sq ft with 30-foot ceilings, for banquets of up to about 1,900 guests and receptions of up to 3,000. It divides into smaller sections, and the Centennial Foyer outside it holds receptions of up to 1,500.
spaces.why: A six-piece band playing 90s and 2000s R&B and hip-hop, for when you want everyone dancing.

spaces.name: Capitol Ballroom
spaces.facts: The Capitol Ballroom has 22-foot ceilings and hand-blown Italian glass light fixtures, for seated events of up to about 1,200.
spaces.why: Stevie Wonder, Aretha Franklin and Motown, for a party where people dance.

spaces.name: Silver Room
spaces.facts: The Silver Room is about 1,200 sq ft with floor-to-ceiling windows, for rehearsal dinners and small receptions.
spaces.why: Upright bass and guitar, at a volume nobody has to raise their voice over.
spaces.alt: The Silver Room set with cocktail tables and flowers, with floor-to-ceiling windows.

props.title: Planning music at Hyatt Regency Denver

rows.text: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space, from a small speaker on the terrace to a full stage system in the Centennial Ballroom.
It’s a big hotel with a lot going on, so we plan load-in with the events team and the convention services staff.
When a big convention is in town, the hotel and the streets around it are busy, so we build in extra time for the act to arrive and set up.
There’s self-parking and valet at the hotel.

props.html: Questions to ask the Hyatt Regency Denver events team

items.html: Which spaces have an end time for amplified music, and when is it?
Does the hotel’s AV team need to connect or run the band’s sound, and is there a fee for that?
Where do vendors load in, and when can the band set up?
Is there power near where the band will play?
What wording do you need on the certificate of insurance?

props.html: Forward this list to the events team, or send us the answers and we’ll plan around them.
Questions about music at Hyatt Regency Denver

items.q: Can we bring our own band to a wedding at Hyatt Regency Denver?
items.a: Hotels like Hyatt Regency Denver generally let you book your own entertainment, within their rules on insurance, load-in and sound. Your event manager can confirm them for your date, and we send a certificate of insurance with every booking.

items.q: Does the band need the hotel’s AV team?
items.a: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The hotel’s AV team can add anything beyond that, and we’ll work out the details with your event manager.

items.q: Can one act play the ceremony, the cocktail hour and the reception?
items.a: Yes. The same act can move with you from The Denver City Terrace to The Silver Room to The Capitol Ballroom, and one booking covers all of it.

items.q: How much does live music add to a wedding at Hyatt Regency Denver?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act and how much of the day it covers. Our pricing page has what live music costs in the Colorado market, and we’ll send a quote for your date.
